$comment: The narrative manifest. Beats are data, not code -- editing the story should not mean editing TypeScript. tools/validate.mjs cross-checks every gate and chapter against what Blender exported, and every line timing against the real length of the voiceover file, so a line scheduled past the end of the audio fails the build.
$timingNote: atMs values were written against the script in content/vo/script.md, then scaled to the delivered takes (arrival 36.75s vs 50s scripted; radio 66.19s vs 96s scripted). Scaling assumes even pacing, which speech is not -- pauses compress differently from words. These are a starting point, not a transcription. Re-time by ear with `?capture=1` and the C key, which prints a corrected array to the console.
title: A Room That Remembers

lines.text: Mind the step. There's always been a step.
Forty-one years, this room. Forty-one years of other people's broken things.
They'd come in under an arm. Wrapped in a tea towel like something that had died.
And I'd say — leave it with me. I always said that.
I never once said I can't. Not out loud.
Look at a thing long enough, and it'll tell you when.
Ah. That one. That one was Mrs Ellery's, two streets over.
Came in with a crack down the back and a hum you could feel in your teeth.
Four evenings, that took me. A valve. A dry joint on the transformer.
And a screw I had to cut myself. They'd stopped making that thread. So I made it.
She couldn't pay. I knew that when she walked in.
She brought bread instead. Every Friday for a year. A loaf on that bench, still warm.
She died in the spring of eighty-six.
And I kept it working. Thirty years, I kept that radio working.
Nobody was listening to it. I knew that. I'm not daft.
But it's a small thing, isn't it. To keep something going. After.
It's the only kind of mending I was ever any good at.
